reuse.why: Generalises getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds isScheduleExcludedDay, but getDatesInRange inlines its own weekend-or-holiday expression right next to an imported isScheduleExcludedDay, and the schedule-template callers of getDateWithSkippedWeekend are not given holidays.

duplication.why: The holiday predicate is restated inline in getDatesInRange, and the daily-skip-versus-shift decision is now written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: The predicate and shift loop live in shared/schedules.ts, but server/schedules/app.ts makes its own daily/holiday decisions instead of delegating them.

scope.why: Focused on schedules, though getUpcomingDates is restructured (over-fetch multiplier, dedup) beyond what the change needs, and long lines are left unformatted.

maintainability.why: The rule is spread over three hand-written branches with magic look-ahead multipliers, and one consumer (budget schedule templates) silently ignores holidays.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange uses `d.isWeekend(date) || config.holidays?.includes(dayFromDate(date))` instead of isScheduleExcludedDay; budget/schedule-template.ts still calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange re-expresses isScheduleExcludedDay inline, and getUpcomingDates rebuilds the daily-skip/shift branch as a flatMap rather than sharing one resolver with getDatesInRange and getNextDate.

one_place.where: The predicate lives in isScheduleExcludedDay (shared/schedules.ts), but getDatesInRange restates it inline and budget/schedule-template.ts never passes holidays, so not every path that applies the rule uses the shared definition.
